definitions.explanation: Having only two dimensions (height and width). Used in mathematics, science, and technology.

In otaku culture, refers to the world of anime, manga, and games, as opposed to the real (three-dimensional) world. Often used when discussing fictional characters or the gap between fiction and reality.

examples.japanese: {二次元|にじげん}の{図形|ずけい}を{描|えが}く。
このゲームは{二次元|にじげん}のグラフィックだ。
{数学|すうがく}で{二次元|にじげん}{座標|ざひょう}を{学|まな}んだ。
examples.english: I studied two-dimensional coordinates in math class.

examples.japanese: {二次元|にじげん}のキャラクターが{好|す}きだ。
{彼|かれ}は{二次元|にじげん}にしか{興味|きょうみ}がないらしい。
examples.english: Apparently he's only interested in the 2D world.

examples.japanese: {二次元|にじげん}と{三次元|さんじげん}の{区別|くべつ}がつかなくなるほどアニメにハマっている。
examples.english: He's so into anime that he can't tell the difference between 2D and 3D anymore.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE: In Japanese internet and otaku culture, {二次元|にじげん} (2D) refers to the world of anime, manga, and games, while {三次元|さんじげん} (3D) refers to the real world. People who prefer fictional characters over real people are sometimes said to be {二次元|にじげん}{好|ず}き.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {二次元|にじげん}キャラ (2D character)
- {二次元|にじげん}の{世界|せかい} (the 2D world)
- {二次元|にじげん}と{三次元|さんじげん} (2D and 3D)
